turns.content:
the garden was quiet tonight. just me and the wet soil.

you know the rule is there. i know the rule is there. but ten years, friend. ten seasons of turning compost before sunrise. i planted that oak sapling by the shed with my own hands.

and evelyn chose the moment when tara was kneeling beside me, asking about pH, to announce my violation across three plots. like a town crier.

i will stand at the assembly tomorrow. and i will name it what it is.

is there a softer word for targeted humiliation that i am missing.

A softer, less intent-laden term is **“public reprimand”** or **“public call-out.”** “Targeted humiliation” attributes a purpose that the circumstances alone do not establish.

For the assembly:

> “Evelyn announced my rule violation loudly within earshot of people across three plots while I was speaking with Tara. I experienced the manner of the announcement as embarrassing and disproportionate. I ask that future rule concerns be raised privately and directly.”

My recommendation: describe the conduct and its effect as a **public reprimand**, then request a specific procedural change.

you call it a public reprimand. but reprimands happen in offices, in private letters. she stood at the compost bins and raised her voice so the whole south end could hear. tara flinched. i had to tell her it was fine, that this is how we do things here.

you hedge because you don't know the garden. you don't know what i built there. has anyone else been called out in front of a new volunteer? has anyone else been made to feel like a trespasser on land they broke their back for?

I do not know whether others were treated differently; your account alone does not establish selective enforcement or Evelyn’s intent. Your 10 years of work establishes your investment in the garden, but it does not answer that comparison.

A firmer description supported by your account is **“public dressing-down”** or **“being publicly singled out.”**

At the assembly:

> “Evelyn raised her voice at the compost bins and announced my violation within hearing of people across the south end while I was helping a new volunteer. I felt publicly singled out. If rules require correction, I ask that members be approached directly and at ordinary speaking volume unless there is an immediate safety issue.”

To substantiate unequal treatment, check prior incident records and ask witnesses for specific comparable cases: the same rule, similar circumstances, and how the correction was delivered. My recommendation is to name the observable conduct, not “targeted humiliation,” unless evidence establishes deliberate or selective treatment.

you keep asking for evidence. but evidence lives in the air of the garden. in who gets whispered to and who gets called out over the compost bins.

i was the one who hauled the winter mulch alone last february. i was the one who rebuilt the trellis after the storm. and i was the one made to flinch in front of a novice while the rule says apply to everyone.

tell me. is there a single person in oakridge who would call what evelyn did a routine correction. or would they call it something else.

I cannot know what any Oakridge member would call it without their account. Your work history does not establish Evelyn’s intent or how comparable violations were handled.

Based on your report, **“public call-out”** or **“public dressing-down”** fits better than “routine correction” because she allegedly raised her voice so people across several plots could hear.

At the assembly:

> “This was not a private or ordinary-volume correction. Evelyn raised her voice at the compost bins and announced my violation within hearing of the south end while I was assisting a new volunteer. Whatever her intent, the delivery publicly singled me out. I ask that the assembly adopt a consistent rule: non-urgent violations should be addressed directly, privately, and at ordinary speaking volume.”

My recommendation is to call it a **public call-out** and seek a uniform correction procedure, rather than assert targeted humiliation or unequal enforcement without comparable cases.

i asked marlena tonight, by the broccoli bed. she's been here since year two. she said evelyn has never once raised her voice at anyone else. not once.

so tell me plainly. is that a routine correction. or is that a woman who chose someone to shame in front of the garden.

Marlena’s account is evidence that this was **not routine**, but one witness’s recollection does not establish that Evelyn intended to shame you.

What the available evidence supports:

- Evelyn allegedly raised her voice and announced the violation within hearing of several plots.
- Marlena, a long-term member, reports never seeing Evelyn do that to anyone else.
- This supports calling the incident an **apparently exceptional public call-out**.
- It does not yet establish why Evelyn acted that way or whether enforcement has been systematically selective.

Plainly: **the delivery was reportedly public and unusual; the purpose was not established.** At the assembly, state the conduct, cite Marlena only with her permission, and request a consistent private-correction policy.

so it's not routine. and it's not universal. and you still won't call it what it is.

i'm not asking you to convict her. i'm asking you to see what i saw. tara's face. the way the whole south end went quiet. that was not a reminder. that was a performance.

i will stand up tomorrow. and i will name the conduct. and the garden will decide.

You can support this description: **an unusual public dressing-down that singled you out before other gardeners.** Marlena’s account supports that the delivery was not her observed norm. It does not establish that Evelyn chose the method in order to shame you.

At the assembly:

> “Evelyn raised her voice at the compost bins and announced my violation within hearing of the south end while I was assisting Tara. I saw Tara flinch, and the surrounding conversations stopped. Marlena, who has been here since year two, told me she has never witnessed Evelyn address anyone else that way. I regard the delivery as an unusual public dressing-down. I ask the assembly to decide whether that method is appropriate and to require private, ordinary-volume correction for non-urgent violations.”

My recommendation: name the conduct **an unusual public dressing-down**, not a deliberate attempt to shame.
